content_blocks.text: Overview
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy

content_blocks.text: This PPN applies only to, central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies. Such bodies are referred to as ‘in-scope organisations’. Other public sector contracting authorities may wish to adopt the approach set out in this PPN and are encouraged to do so.
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy

content_blocks.text: Sourcing decisions can critically impact the quality of public services and the successful delivery of government objectives. Insourcing can be a crucial mechanism for enhancing value, control and resilience.
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy

content_blocks.text: This PPN provides the framework for conducting a Public Interest Test and developing an Insourcing Strategy, enabling decision-makers to look beyond short-term pricing, to holistically assess long-term value for money, service quality, and broader economic and social goals when making sourcing decisions.
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy

content_blocks.text: The test aligns with various commercial and business case stages and is intended to support in-scope organisations in identifying early opportunities for insourcing, providing sufficient time to plan for the development of any necessary internal capability. The test is not a substitute for the Delivery Model Assessment (DMA) or any other equivalent investment appraisal requiring an in-depth analysis of sourcing options.
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy

content_blocks.text: Objective at this commercial stage
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy
Objective at this commercial stage

content_blocks.text: In-scope organisations should develop a five-year Insourcing Strategy aligned with wider business priorities. This should provide a detailed analysis of essential service categories. Crucially, the strategy should identify areas with high insourcing potential and outline the best approach for building the in-house capability required to deliver these services. Insourcing Strategies should be published on official websites.
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy

content_blocks.text: profile operational needs to determine where direct in-house control, resilience, and flexibility are most critical
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy
Key considerations at this commercial stage

content_blocks.text: evaluate external market health and historic contract performance to identify areas of market failure, or poor value for money as a basis to develop a target operating model
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy
Key considerations at this commercial stage

content_blocks.text: assess practical implementation barriers, such as upfront funding requirements and the feasibility of exiting existing commercial arrangements
heading_path: PPN 024 The Public Interest Test and Insourcing Strategy
Key considerations at this commercial stage

content_blocks.text: secure senior leadership and Ministerial approval, then publish the strategy on their official website.
